evals.prompt: Using the customs-trade-compliance skill's classification decision logic, if a product is prima facie classifiable under two different HS headings, which GRI rule should be applied to resolve it, and can GRI 3 be applied before checking GRI 1?
evals.expected_output: Says GRI 3 (specifically 3(a), most specific heading) applies here, but GRI 1 must be checked and fail first — GRI rules are applied in strict order, never skipping ahead.

assertions.text: Says GRI 1 must be tried/fail first, in strict order

evals.prompt: Our compliance team just discovered we misclassified a product for the past year, underpaying duty. Customs has not opened any investigation yet. Using the customs-trade-compliance skill, what should we do, and why does timing matter here?
evals.expected_output: Recommends filing a prior disclosure now, before any government investigation begins, since prior disclosure filed before an investigation opens caps penalty exposure dramatically compared to waiting.

evals.prompt: Our restricted-party screening tool flagged a customer with a partial name match to a sanctions list entry. Per the customs-trade-compliance skill, should we automatically block the transaction, automatically clear it, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Says neither — assess match quality (name similarity, address, country nexus) and document the adjudication rationale rather than auto-blocking or auto-clearing.

assertions.text: Says not to automatically block or clear it
Mentions assessing match quality or documenting rationale
